The key prerequisite for SIMD optimization is that data must be stored contiguously ^. However, RHS rows within the window are not contiguous (scattered across page frames), so an extra one-time pass is needed to copy values into a per-key contiguous buffer. This design trade-off is worth noting ^:
| Factor | Impact |
|--------|--------|
| Extra RHS column reads | Each RHS column is read twice (buffer copy + aggregation consumption) |
| SIMD bound | If the input is contiguous, the aggregation loop is SIMD-bound; otherwise it is call-bound, with AVX2 providing roughly a 10x advantage |
| Memory prefetch | RHS columns are read sequentially, friendly to the memory subsystem |
| Cache locality | Per-key value buffer size scales with the RHS slice of the current LHS frame, keeping the working set in L2/L3 |
For low-cardinality scenarios (few distinct keys), per-key value buffers fit in cache, and the buffer-copy cost is fully offset. Benchmarks confirm that even small frames beat the scalar path, and the gap widens as the LHS frame grows (more LHS rows share the same index buffer).
